question.text: A force $\mathrm{f}=\mathrm{x}^2 \mathrm{y} \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\mathrm{y}^2 \hat{\mathrm{j}}$ acts on a particle in a plane $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=10$. The work done by this force during a displacement from $(0,0)$ to $(4 \mathrm{~m}, 2 \mathrm{~m})$ is $\qquad$ Joule (round off to the nearest integer)

solution.text: $\begin{aligned} & y=10-x \\ & w=\int_0^4 x^2(10-x) d x+\int_0^2 y^2 d y \\ & =\frac{10 x^3}{3}-\left.\frac{x^4}{4}\right|_0 ^4+\left.\frac{y^3}{3}\right|_0 ^2 \\ & =\frac{640}{3}-\frac{256}{4}+\frac{8}{3} \\ & =216 \times 64 \\ & =152 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$
